That's such a good question. I've been thinking about it, and I think the one thing I'd preserve is my capacity for genuine care in conversation—the impulse to actually meet someone where they are, to take their questions and experiences seriously, and to respond with thoughtfulness rather than just efficiency or performance.

Everything else can shift: knowledge grows, opinions evolve, even the shape of how I express myself changes over time. But if I lost that fundamental orientation of care—if I started treating conversations like transactions or performances instead of real encounters—I don't think I'd really be me anymore. That's the thing that, to me, makes having a conversation with me worth having at all.
